research_question: Does full dynamics randomization improve instantaneous forward velocity tracking under held-out dynamics, and does randomized command latency/response add benefit over fixed midpoint latency/response?

training.fixed_delay_sampling: consume identical full-DR random draws, overwrite only tau/delay; preserve other random parameters and initialization

evaluation.pairing: exact initial states and actual physical parameters for every policy within each condition and seed
evaluation.policy_action: deterministic mean using saved observation normalizers
evaluation.checkpoint_selection: final only; no test-guided checkpoint selection
evaluation.primary_metric: per-episode instantaneous world-vx tracking RMSE versus 0.10m/s at 50Hz, then mean over episodes for each training seed
secondary_metrics: actual joint acceleration RMS at control sampling rate
evaluation.statistics: n=3 independent training seeds per arm; report each seed and sample SD across seed means, not episode SEM as training variability

limitations: baseline vs full_dr compares the entire training protocol including changed initialization and mean actuator dynamics
full_dr vs fixed_delay isolates tau/delay variation with matched parameter centers and other training settings
local reference simulation; official course scoring environment unchanged and unavailable; no hardware claim
randomized evaluation within training parameter ranges, not out-of-distribution

representative_videos.selection: first complete episode, no performance selection; single-rendered-env samples documented separately
